one_liner: Template-metaprogrammed C++ geometric algebra library; within ~15% of GATL and 18-2,600x faster than Garamon, TbGAL, GluCat.
what_it_does: Versor (libvsr) is a C++11 geometric (Clifford) algebra library: typed multivectors for any metric and dimension (vsr::nga generic, vsr::cga for 3D conformal GA with named types such as Point, Vec, Biv, Rotor, Motor, Circle, Sphere), combined with overloaded operators (* geometric product, ^ outer, <= left contraction, ! inverse, ~ reverse, % commutator) and helpers like Construct::point and Gen:: rotor/motor generators. It models points, lines, circles, spheres and the rigid-body and conformal transformations that act on them, with optional OpenGL/GLES drawing and GUI examples. It is not a drop-in for any matrix, quaternion or computational-geometry API; adopting it means writing your geometry in GA terms.
how_it_is_fast: Each multivector type carries its list of basis blades as a template parameter, and products are expanded at compile time: vsr_products.h enumerates blade pairs with bitmask tests (xor for the result blade, sign-flip, inner/outer legality), builds an instruction list for only the non-zero coefficient pairs, and deduces the sparse result type, so a * b compiles to a fixed sequence of multiply-adds over a plain value_t val[N] array with no runtime dispatch or heap. Conformal null-basis metrics are handled by a compile-time split to a diagonal Minkowski basis (vsr_split_met.h). This is the same compile-time code-generation family as GATL, Gaalet (expression templates) and Gaalop (precompiler), which is why those four cluster within about 15% of each other while runtime-dispatched Garamon, TbGAL and GluCat are one to three orders of magnitude slower.
when_to_use: Conformal GA (3D CGA) or 2-5D Euclidean/Minkowski algebra in C++ where dimensions and blade layouts are known at compile time and you want typed sparse multivectors with no runtime overhead

Replacing a runtime-dispatched GA library: in the 2020 ga-benchmark run Versor's per-call wall-clock time was 18x (Garamon), 37x (TbGAL), 162x (GluCat framed) and 2,588x (GluCat matrix) lower on geometric mean over shared cases (derived from page data)
Normalization-heavy code: runit() measured about 3.4x faster than GATL's normalization on geometric mean (derived from page data)
Robotics, kinematics or parametric-design prototypes that benefit from the built-in OpenGL/GLES drawing and example apps
Projects that need a permissive licence (BSD-2-Clause) for GA code
when_not_to_use: You want the fastest compile-time GA library: in the same run GATL was faster in 1,239 of 1,816 shared cases (about 1.14x geometric mean) and 3.5x faster on the conformal inverse-kinematics algorithm (242 ns vs 857 ns per call, derived from page data)
Commutator-product-heavy code: operator% computes (ab - ba)/2 with two full geometric products and measured about 2.5x slower than GATL
You need operations ga-benchmark found missing: right contraction, regressive product, dot and Hestenes inner products were marked not implemented (a scalar_product method exists in current devel)

Higher or runtime-chosen dimensions: blade lists are compile-time types, the build needs -ftemplate-depth-1200, compile times grow with dimension, and issue #22 reports the Rotor typedef is incomplete above 3D (no pseudoscalar)
You need a Boost.Geometry/CGAL/GEOS replacement: no robust predicates, polygons, meshes or spatial indexes, and no benchmark against those incumbents

integration.form: static lib (product core is header templates in include/vsr; libvsr/vsr_shared are built with CMake from src/space/*.cpp for CGA helper functions, and ga-benchmark links libvsr)
integration.dependencies: none for the math core; GLEW plus the ext/gfx submodule (GL/GLES, GLV/imgui) for graphics; ext/gtest submodule for tests
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (README: gcc 4.7+ or clang 3.2+), CMake 3.10, -ftemplate-depth-1200; clang 20.1.8 compile errors fixed in PR #33 (Nov 2025)
integration.platforms: README says tested on Linux and macOS; CMake also has Windows and Raspberry Pi (GLES) branches and a 2024 commit mentions an Android build; portable scalar C++ with no SIMD intrinsics in the core headers read
integration.thread_safety: not documented; multivectors are plain value types over fixed arrays and no shared mutable state was seen in the core headers (only static basis constants)

gotchas: Harness flaw behind the recorded medal table: ga-benchmark ranks by mean CPU time (USED_METRIC = 'cpu_time' in gabm.py), but on the WSL1 host the CPU clock advances in 15.625 ms ticks while each 10,000-call repetition takes only about 20-200 microseconds, so 89% of Versor's measured cases (92% of GATL's, 92-93% of Gaalop's and Gaalet's) record exactly 0.0 CPU time; golds are ties at zero (1,042 golds over 324 cases in my reproduction from the run's JSON files) and a silver means one tick happened to land in one of 30 repetitions (5.2e-05 ms = 15.625 ms / 10,000 / 30). Re-ranked by the high-resolution real_time stored in the same files, golds are GATL 111, Gaalet 76, Gaalop 55, Versor 23 (derived from page data).

operator! computes ~A / (A ~A)[0], which is a correct inverse only for blades and versors, and silently returns the reverse when that scalar is 0; runit() returns a zero multivector for null input and norm() clamps negative weights to 0.
Assigning between multivector types compiles and silently drops components: issue #20 (open) shows vector e1e2 = e1*e2 yielding zero; use auto or the exact product type.
operator<= is the left contraction (zero when the left grade exceeds the right), not a symmetric dot product.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the catalogued geometry-spatial siblings is a geometric algebra library: they are predicates, triangulation, spatial indexes, mesh booleans and physics engines (CGAL, Boost.Geometry, nanoflann, Manifold, Jolt). Pick Versor only to express rigid-body and conformal transformations of points, lines, circles and spheres algebraically, and pair it with one of those siblings for spatial queries.
verified_claims_summary: ga-benchmark's 2020-02-05 run (GCC 7.4.0, CMake Release, double precision, Google Benchmark with 10,000 calls x 30 repetitions on random blades, 8 x 1992 MHz CPUs under WSL1, CPU model not stated) gives Versor 246/76/1 medals by mean CPU time, level with GATL, but almost all those golds are zero-CPU-time ties caused by the 15.625 ms WSL1 clock. The run's own wall-clock data put Versor at about 0.88x GATL's speed and 0.96-0.98x Gaalop's and Gaalet's on geometric mean, and 18x to 2,588x faster than Garamon, TbGAL and GluCat over the cases both implement (derived from page data); nothing is compared with Boost.Geometry, CGAL, GEOS or a std facility.
status_note: Active on the default devel branch (last commit 2025-11-03 merging an outside contributor's clang 20 fixes; most 2024-2025 commits are graphics demos), BSD-2-Clause and usable as a math-only library, but its only independent speed evidence is a 2020 run whose CPU-time medal table is a timer-resolution artifact; the same run's wall-clock data support 'close to the fastest GA template libraries', not 'fastest'.
